clue.text: Inexhaustible criminal in Sligo? Not so

indicators.note: the criminal is placed inside what remains of the Irish town's name
'Not so' tells us to remove the letters of the word so from the place name

parts.note: a felon is a criminal

explanation.surface: A question about whether an inexhaustible offender is at large in the Irish town of Sligo.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'Not so' read like a denial of the crime, but 'Not' strips the letters of 'so' from the town's name, and 'in' puts the criminal inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifelong lasts a whole lifetime and so never runs out, as an inexhaustible supply would.

clue.text: Threaten to include seaman's work

indicators.note: the threatening word takes the sailor inside it

parts.note: to lour is to look threatening, as a dark sky does
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Intimidating a sailor into doing his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts the sailor inside the verb; lour (also spelt lower) describes a sky that threatens rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is hard physical work or effort.

clue.text: Beauty treatment making the front of many papers

parts.note: the face is the front of something
C is the Roman numeral for 100, so it stands for many
a ream is a quantity of paper sheets

explanation.surface: A cosmetics advert splashed across the front pages of the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' suggests newspapers, but a ream is 500 sheets; 'making' and 'of' link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Face cream is a cosmetic applied to the skin, a beauty treatment.

clue.text: Minimum time on the fields

indicators.note: here time is placed after the fields, as if the fields carried it on their end

parts.note: leas are meadows or fields

explanation.surface: The shortest spell spent out in the meadows.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAS is the poetic word for meadows.
explanation.definitionFit: The least is the smallest amount possible, the minimum.

clue.text: Composer composed "Nine Lives" (minus four)

indicators.note: something composed has been put together anew, so the letters are rearranged
minus means taken away, so the Roman numeral for four comes out

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A composer wrote a piece called Nine Lives, less a few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minus four' removes IV from NINELIVES to leave NINELES, which 'composed' rearranges. Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer of symphonies and concertos.

clue.text: Undisturbed by origins of pastrycook's lemon tart

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so the opening letters of the two following words are taken

parts.note: tart means sour, acid

explanation.surface: A calm customer unruffled by a baker's lemon tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins of' takes P and L, the first letters of 'pastrycook's' and 'lemon'; 'tart' is an adjective here, sour, not a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid describes a calm, untroubled temperament, the state of being undisturbed.

clue.text: What to do if you don't like sweet tea?

definitions.text: What to do if you don't like sweet tea?

parts.words: What to do if you don't like sweet tea?
parts.note: read as a lump of sugar in the cup, or as the advice to put up with it, to lump it

explanation.definitionFit: Lumps of sugar go into tea, and to lump something is to accept what you dislike.

clue.text: Man upholding one lady

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Man upholding one lady (5)' with answer CELTA: CELT + A builds the letters, but CELTA is not a lady and no other word or crossing explains the definition; the clue or answer looks garbled.

clue.text: Scatter and swim, absorbing second language

indicators.note: the swim soaks up the letter for second, which goes inside it

parts.note: a dip is a short swim
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: Breaking up and going for a swim while picking up another tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' puts S inside DIP; Erse is Irish or Scottish Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: To disperse is to scatter in different directions.

clue.text: Live animal eating hot sauce

parts.note: to live is to be

indicators.note: the animal swallows the letter for hot, which goes inside it

parts.note: a camel is an animal
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A living creature gobbling up a spicy sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts H inside the animal; 'Live' is the verb to be, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Béchamel is the classic French white sauce made from milk, butter and flour.

clue.text: Offal with edges trimmed — most modest

indicators.note: trimming the edges cuts off the first and last letters of the synonym for most modest

parts.note: the most modest person is the humblest

explanation.surface: Offal whose edges have been neatly cut, served to the meekest diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with edges trimmed' takes the first and last letters off HUMBLEST. Umbles are the edible innards of a deer, the origin of 'humble pie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbles are the heart, liver and entrails of a deer or other animal, eaten as food.

clue.text: With which saying something seasonal is problematic

definitions.text: With which saying something seasonal is problematic

indicators.note: something of the phrase is just a part of it, so the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A speech defect that trips up anyone trying to say a festive word.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and 'something' points to the letters running across 'seasonaL IS Problematic'; 'seasonal' is full of the s sounds a lisp spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech defect that sounds s as th makes a word with many s sounds hard to pronounce.

clue.text: University teachers admit head of college is telling the whole story

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so the college's first letter goes inside the union's letters

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: University staff letting a college principal in, and nothing held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admit' places C, from 'head of college', inside NUT. The NUT was Britain's National Union of Teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncut version of a film or story is complete, giving every part without omissions.

clue.text: Well-turned-out joints (by chance) in the Home Counties

indicators.note: both pieces sit inside the abbreviation for the region named

parts.note: the Home Counties are the counties around London in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
hips are joints
hap is an old word for chance or luck

explanation.surface: Smartly dressed people whose joints happen to be in the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts both pieces inside SE. The Home Counties are the counties around London, in England's South East; hap is an old word for luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape means neat and in good order, as a well-turned-out person or place is.

clue.text: Writer on edge of pot

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another follows it, so the writer comes after the edge

parts.note: the hem is the edge of a garment
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: An author perched on the rim of a cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' is cannabis, not a cooking vessel; hemp is the plant, so hempen means made of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hempen means made from hemp, the cannabis plant also smoked as marijuana.

clue.text: Quietly involve mystic symbol

parts.note: P, piano, means quietly in music
to entangle someone is to involve them

explanation.surface: Discreetly drawing someone into an occult sign.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the musical marking piano, meaning quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentangle is a five-pointed star used as a magical or occult symbol.

clue.text: Legendary high-flier returned drink containing herb

indicators.note: something returned is sent back, so the whole assembly is read from right to left
the drink holds the herb inside it

parts.note: to sup is to drink
sage is a culinary herb

explanation.surface: A mythical aviator sent back a herbal drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts the herb inside the drink, and 'returned' reverses the whole assembly, giving the winged horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegasus is the winged horse of Greek myth, a legendary creature that flew.

clue.text: The fuss or disturbance resulting from a quick temper

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs things up, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Commotion and upset brought on by someone who flares up easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' signals the anagram of THE FUSS OR; 'resulting from' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a short fuse loses their temper quickly, like a bomb that goes off soon after lighting.

clue.text: Mary and I upset the farmhand

indicators.note: upsetting something knocks it over, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Mary and I have annoyed the farm worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an emotion, but it rearranges MARY AND I.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairyman works on a dairy farm, milking and tending cows.

clue.text: Mrs Mahler is able to reject the Book of the Year

parts.note: Alma Mahler was the wife of the composer Gustav Mahler

indicators.note: rejecting something throws it back, so the word for is able is reversed

parts.note: if one is able one can

explanation.surface: The composer's wife turns down a book award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reject' reverses the verb. Alma Mahler was Gustav Mahler's wife; the 'Book of the Year' is not a prize but an annual reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual publication giving the calendar and facts for that year.

clue.text: Shell suit

definitions.meaning: a lawsuit, an action brought in court

explanation.definitionFit: A case is an outer shell or covering, and in law a case is a suit brought to court.

clue.text: Farm vehicle on the box

parts.note: a cart is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A tractor or wagon appearing on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the box' reads as being on TV; 'the box' is the definition, a cardboard container.
explanation.definitionFit: A carton is a light cardboard container, a kind of box.

clue.text: Disreputable character with claim on body

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
to aver is to state or claim

explanation.surface: A rogue laying claim to a body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a corpse, a dead body.

clue.text: Icy cold, unlike the Netherlands

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the Netherlands is famously flat, so unlike it is hilly

explanation.surface: Freezing weather, quite different from Dutch conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Icy cold' looks like one phrase, but 'cold' gives C and the definition is 'Icy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilly means cold and frosty, close to icy.

clue.text: Polished coffin-bearer in danger

indicators.note: the coffin-bearer is placed inside the colour for danger

parts.note: red is the colour of danger signals
a hearse is the vehicle that carries a coffin

explanation.surface: A funeral pall-bearer finds themselves in peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coffin-bearer' suggests a pall-bearer, but it is the funeral vehicle; 'in' puts it inside the colour of danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsed performance has been practised until it is smooth, polished and ready.

clue.text: Added colour to a layer of sodium

parts.note: a hen is a layer of eggs
Na is the chemical symbol for sodium

explanation.surface: Tinting a coat of sodium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' reads as a coating, but it is something that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye used to put colour into hair and skin.

clue.text: N Many hanker for the gutter

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, so it stands for many
to hanker is to itch for something

explanation.surface: Lots of people long for the lowest point in life.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray N in the printed clue is an OCR fragment. Roman numerals such as D (500) commonly stand for 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditch is a channel dug to carry water, much as a gutter does along a road.

clue.text: Material that gets dug up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: mined means dug out of the ground

explanation.surface: Stuff that is excavated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses MINED in this down clue; 'that gets' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton cloth, a material used for jeans.

clue.text: Succeed in becoming adult and mature

parts.note: a man is an adult male
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Making a go of growing up and maturing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in becoming' joins the pieces; 'mature' is a verb here, to age.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage is to succeed in doing something, often against difficulty.

clue.text: Leave nut roast though long-awaited

indicators.note: roasting cooks the letters, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Give up the nut roast even though you have waited so long for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roast' is the anagram signal, cooking up LEAVE NUT into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eventual happens in the end, after a long wait for it to arrive.

clue.text: Set in order when quarter-consumed

parts.note: N, north, is one of the four quarters of the compass
food consumed has been eaten

explanation.surface: Tidying up after a quarter of the meal has been eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter' is a compass point, here N.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten something is to tidy it, putting it in proper order.

clue.text: Attempt to include bottom note in Pomp and Circumstance?

indicators.note: the attempt takes in the other pieces, which go inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
the rump is the bottom
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A try at slipping a low note into Elgar's famous march.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar's 'Pomp and Circumstance' marches are the surface picture; the question mark marks pomp as an example of showy, empty display. 'to include' puts the two pieces inside the attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpery is showy but worthless display, the empty side of pomp and ceremony.
